items.q: What if I don't know my exact time of birth?
items.a: We'll cast the chart for noon. The positions of the Sun, planets and most aspects stay accurate, but we can't calculate houses and the Ascendant — those sections are skipped. The time is often on your birth certificate or hospital records.

items.q: How is this different from a horoscope?
items.a: A horoscope describes one twelfth of humanity by Sun sign. A birth chart is the position of ten planets, the Ascendant and houses at the moment you were born, and the angles between them. Two people with the same sign get two different texts from us.

The calculation is done by software using the Swiss Ephemeris. The text is composed by a language model following a method written by Natalka's astrologers; every paragraph is tied to a specific position or aspect in your chart.

items.q: How do you store my data?
items.a: Your date, time and place of birth are stored only to build your documents and are deleted after 30 days. We don't share them with third parties.
